subject: Key wrapping proxy design for BYOK private deployments
messages:
From: Luke Harrington <luke.h@vantagehealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: secops@vantagehealth.com
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 13:18:00 -0700
Subject: Private BYOK — key wrapping proxy & rotation questions

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the private deployment walkthrough was helpful. Our security team has a few follow-ups before we sign off on the network design:

1) We need a clear diagram and operations model for the BYOK path when our master key (customer-owned) is used. Specifically: who performs wrapping/unwrapping, where plaintext ever exists, and how rotations are handled without downtime.

2) Escrow and escape-hatch requirements: we have an internal policy that requires an escrow plan (3rd-party or threshold split) for master-key recovery if the customer loses access. We also need attestations for any transfer.

3) Operator/roles separation: SRE vs HSM operator vs app teams — our auditors want to see role separation and logged attestations.

Can your team provide an architecture sketch + an ops playbook describing the wrapping proxy, rotation windows, and escrow process?

Appreciate a concise design note we can attach to our procurement docs.

— Luke
SecOps Lead, Vantage Health
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Luke Harrington <luke.h@vantagehealth.com>
Cc: tessa.morgan@redwood.com, hiro.tanaka@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 16:42:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Private BYOK — key wrapping proxy & rotation questions

Hi Luke — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a concise package to cover each ask and proposing a small follow-up call if anything needs clarification. High-level answers below; details in the attached diagram and YAML flow.

Summary (short):
- We never persist customer plaintext on Redwood hosts. Customer master keys are only used to create short-lived wrapping keys via an ephemeral Key Wrapping Proxy (KWP). The KWP performs a PKCS#11 / KMIP attested session to the customer HSM (or cloud KMS) to request a one-time wrap of the per-tenant data-encryption key (DEK).
- DEKs are stored encrypted in the customer VPC storage (or on-prem vault) and are rewrapped during rotation using a rolling rewrap strategy to avoid downtime.
- Escrow: we support a threshold-split escrow (Shamir 3-of-5 by default) that can be stored in a customer-controlled escrow service or in an audited third-party lockbox. All escrow retrievals require multi-party attestation and DocuSign-tracked agreements.
- Operator separation: HSM operator accounts have the ability to manage the HSM appliance (firmware, slot configs) but do not have KMS-level wrap/unwrap privileges for tenant DEKs. The KWP holds the minimal cloud principal that can request wrap operations and records attestation tokens for every operation.

Attachments included (short):
- private-deploy-kms-proxy-v1.pdf (diagram + sequence)
- wrap-flow.yaml (example KWP handshake + rewrap job config)
- operator-roles-matrix.xlsx (who can do what + required attestations)

A few operational notes you may find useful:
- Ephemeral wrapping keys TTL: default 15 minutes, configurable per-deployment (short TTL reduces blast radius).
- Rewrap window: we recommend staggered rewraps across shard groups with <1% traffic shift per shard to keep tail latency predictable.
- Audit evidence: each wrap/unwrap includes a signed attestation blob (KWP signs with a hardware-backed signing key) which we attach to the audit log entry and expose via the Console or a signed S3 export.

If that looks good, we can: 1) add your procurement/security contact to the DocuSign escrow template we use, and 2) schedule a 30m deep-dive to walk the YAML flow and required network ports.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Manager, Private Deployments — Redwood Inference

Luke — quick operational addendum from the on-call/ops perspective:

Operational playbook (high level):
- Preflight: KWP attestation onboarding (exchange of attestation certs + whitelist of HSM endpoints).
- Daily: healthcheck (KWP attestation check + wrap/unwrap latency SLOs).
- Rotation run: trigger rewrap job in Canary -> stagger through 10%/33%/100% windows across shards. Each stage must pass integrity checks (hash/length checks on rewrapped DEKs) before proceeding.
- Emergency escape hatch (customer-initiated): signed offline transfer. Steps: 1) customer triggers escrow release with 2-of-3 customer signatories, 2) escrow coordinator initiates multi-party attestation, 3) KWP issues ephemeral unwrap token which is logged and time-limited, 4) re-encrypt DEKs to customer-provided import key and transfer via HSM-exported wrapped object.

SRE notes on permissions:
- KWP service account role: kms:WrapKey, kms:SignAttestation only. No kms:Decrypt/cross-tenant privileges.
- Operator accounts: can manage HSM runtime but must not have permissions to request DEK unwraps for tenants. Those requests must be signed and proxied through a ticketed, auditable workflow.

I'll include a short runbook excerpt in the next revision that maps specific CLI commands + sample logs.

—Tessa

Adding a few HSM-specific constraints and SOC evidence suggestions from the applied-crypto side:

HSM & firmware constraints:
- Use FIPS-validated HSMs with tamper-evident logs. For on-prem HSMs we recommend module-level attestation and firmware snapshot checks during onboarding.
- The KWP should call into the HSM via an audited PKCS#11 session using ephemeral credentials (derived via an attested bootstrap). No long-lived operator credentials that can call Decrypt at scale.

Escrow wording suggestion (for your procurement):
"In the event of customer key loss, the parties shall follow a threshold-based escrow retrieval procedure: retrieval requires (i) presentation of pre-registered signatory tokens from at least three (3) authorized customer agents; (ii) execution of the third-party escrow release form (DocuSign transaction ID provided); and (iii) a multi-party attestation ceremony logged and retained for audit for at least five (5) years."

Evidence for auditors:
- Signed attestation blobs for wrap/unwrap ops (include non-repudiation headers).
- Firmware/firmware-hash snapshots from HSM onboarding.
- Export of related Console audit logs (CSV) with attestation token IDs.

I'll also drop a brief template for the DocuSign escrow release language into the Drive link. If you want, we can pre-seed the DocuSign with Vantage's procurement contact so the legal teams can iterate.

-Hiro
